research_question: Does a constrained lag-aware full-window loss improve the CR_RVS continuous ECG branch of the full-balanced REM refinement model?
hypothesis: Adding a small lag-aware PCC/L1 loss will improve full-window PCC and RR timing over q1_crrvs_remalign_refine_fullbalanced_fold01_pilot without degrading Shape-200 morphology.
protocol: Fold-01 subject-independent 5-fold CV pilot, CW-STFT input, no target-subject calibration.
changed_variable: Enable constrained lag-aware full-window loss while keeping the refine architecture and full-balanced Shape-200 loss settings fixed.
success_criteria: Full-window PCC exceeds the full-balanced refine fold01 PCC 0.5455.
RR error improves below the full-balanced refine fold01 RR error 21.7 ms.
Shape-200 PCC remains near or above 0.88.
If it does not exceed CW-STFT+TCN fold01 PCC 0.5651 and RR error 14.1 ms, keep as pilot.
checkpoint_selection: Use the training script's validation-best checkpoint only; no test-set checkpoint selection.
failure_interpretation: If lag-aware loss does not improve full-window metrics, the next step should be explicit morphology-to-window assembly or distillation from CW-STFT+TCN rather than more loss tuning.
